title: Keep the order line price exactly as Shopify sends it (no rounding to 2 decimals)
reason: Upstream rounds every unit price to 2 decimals. Currencies with three minor units (ISO 4217: KWD, BHD, JOD, OMR, TND) carry prices such as 12.345, which upstream turns into 12.35: the NetSuite order then has a different amount than the Shopify order. An input adapter cannot fix this because the input is already correct; the loss happens inside upstream code.
originalBehavior: src/mapping.js:11 — unitPrice: round2(Number(l.price)) (price rounded to 2 decimals).
replacementBehavior: src/mapping.js:11 — unitPrice: Number(l.price) (price kept as the decimal Shopify sent; Shopify amounts are already at currency precision).
providerEvidence: ISO 4217 defines three minor-unit digits for KWD, BHD, JOD, OMR and TND.
Shopify sends line prices as decimal strings at the currency's precision (REST line_items[].price, GraphQL originalUnitPriceSet.shopMoney.amount).
Fixture scenario: a KWD order with price 12.345. Not verified against a live Shopify store or NetSuite account.
assumptions: Shopify amounts are exact decimals at currency precision; no further rounding is needed before NetSuite.
NetSuite accepts line rates with more than 2 decimals (rates are not limited to currency precision).
For 2-decimal prices the patched code produces the same numbers as the original (verified by regression replay).
validation: Base file hash equals the pinned upstream file; result hash equals this reviewed patch.
Every other upstream file is unchanged.
Regression: every stored order maps to exactly the same canonical order with and without the patch.
Held orders map without error and their prices equal Shopify's own order record exactly.
Rollback target: the original artifact loads and its files match the pinned commit.
rollback: Rolling back deactivates the patch; the next execution selects the original artifact (installed upstream package, unchanged). Orders already written are not rewritten.
